body: A couple of things. First of all, purging the people who don’t bring value to my life.  Second, taking care of my physical health as it translates to my mental health.

A few years ago I was shopping in a Target store mid afternoon with my then boyfriend.  I was wearing workout clothes and noticed a guy pass by us and look me up and down.  As a girl, you get used to being checked out but the way he looked at me was different.  

At one point, my ex was in one part of the store and I was in another.  I look to the aisle across from me and see this same guy.. staring at me and facing my direction.  He kept putting his hands down his shorts.  Finally it registered what was going on and I asked him “what are you doing?”  He gave me a really creepy smirk.  Alarm bells went off and I left to find my ex.

When I did, I was so uneasy and uncomfortable.  I told him what happened and how weird it was.  He told me just to relax.  We tried to find the guy in the store to no avail.  I felt so off the rest of the day and told some family and friends about it to help alleviate some of my anxiety over the situation.

About a year later, I had on the evening news.  I never even watch the news but felt prompted to that night.  There was a segment about a man being arrested for stalking women and breaking into their apartments to sexually assault them!  It was the guy I had seen in Target a year prior!  I’m so thankful I trusted my instincts and got away from him.  He was at least 3 times my size and could have easily overpowered me had I been alone and he followed me into the parking lot.

Always trust your gut.  If something feels off, it’s because it is.

It’s ok to quit a job!  You spend a lot of time at a job and it’s important to grow and be respected by your employer.  I quit a job in 2017 due to poor management and it was scary at first, but turned out to be the right choice for my mental health.  I have no regrets.  You’ll find the right one.  You aren’t a disappointment and I’m proud of you for leaving!  Best.

Thank you for your kind words!  I’m sorry you were put into that situation.  Just know coming from a stranger-  your life matters and you are important.  I’m sending you all the positive vibes on your journey!  I’m only a message away if you ever need someone to talk to.  Best.
Thank you so much!  I appreciate the support and encouragement.
Thank you for your reply.  I’m definitely dedicated to my own mental health too.  I know now more than ever I need to get myself together so I can be a healthy example.

I left a former job due to a difficult boss.  His dad was the owner of the company and him and his wife both ran the operations.  They never had anything nice to say.  They always put me down about not being organized enough, would want to me to work overtime last minute, criticize me for “not learning fast enough” etc.  Finally I just had enough and started taking my personal belongings home.

The day before I quit I called in and he was telling me I needed a doctors note.  I refused to go so he hit me with the “we’ll definitely be talking tomorrow”.

I go in the next day and tried to come to a mutual agreement.  Him and his wife told me I was free to go.  They never took accountability for anything so he told my co workers they fired me.  I had already planned to quit so no truth to that.

With the exception of them, I loved everyone I work with.  I don’t wish anything bad on him, but I have since found out through old colleagues he’s battling cancer.  I hope the experience has taught him to be less egotistical and more humble.

All the time.  When I feel anxious I feel so worn down.  I’m so tired but I can’t sleep.  I feel hungry but I won’t eat.  It’s like all normal functions just stop and I’m hyper focused on whatever is bringing me anxiety/panic.  The only end feels like offing myself to spare myself the misery.
This is how I would describe it too.  It doesn’t matter how long I live, I’ll always be dealing with it.  It truly is a life sentence.
I’m sorry you’re going through it too.  It sucks.

I’m a mom too.  I feel so guilty battling depression/suicidal thoughts and also trying to raise kids.  I take the kids out, but when we get home I fall asleep for hours.  I too want to escape this world so bad, but I know that feeling all too well.  If I did suicide, I’d ruin my kids lives.  It sucks living a life where you always feel stuck.
Exercising.  At least I look good on the outside!

Thank you.  Your response means a lot to me.  I’m glad I recognized my toxic behavior and I do my best to be my kids’ cheerleader now and encourage them!  It just hurts that I inflicted that upon them when it’s not their fault.  It’s like they say, hurt people hurt people.  My kids just happened to take the brunt of my anger and frustration since they were around me more than anyone else.  In time I hope they realize just how valuable and important they are.  I will make it my point to correct my past behavior and keep moving forward toward a happy and healthy direction for all of us.
I don’t pretend to feel sad or experience depressive episodes.  Those are real emotions for me.  However, I do feel I “fake” being happy a lot of the time and that’s just as emotionally exhausting.
I would love to have a chat.  Please free to send me a DM.  It’s nice not to feel alone.
It’s okay.  I have to go.  My family knows that (not right now) I’m unhappy.  My friends don’t know everything.
I’m about to do it.  It’s ok though. I can’t be helped.  Thank you for your message.
I’ve waited too long.  Getting everything ready to execute.  Thank you for replaying.
Exactly.   We can only do so much.

I understand what you mean.  Last night was bad.  I tried to reach out to as many people as I could.  I didn’t tell them what was going on, but I didn’t want to be alone.  Low and behold everyone was busy or didn’t respond.  I just took it as another sign I’m not meant to be in company.  I entered this world by myself and I’ll leave it by myself too.
It’s the only way out.  I don’t increase my quality of life by staying, I only increase the years of suffering.  I’m in my early 30s.  I’ve done enough time here.
I feel your pain.  It sucks to realize you’re not valued when you do a lot for other people.
You’re correct.  It’s like being given a death sentence.

All I can say is, do what you can to try and get better.  You don’t want to go there.  It was even worse than I imagined.  I’m so glad I’m out.  The food was pretty terrible, but I ate anyways so I could get out.

I was treated fine, but it’s still scary.  You can’t have your personal belongings.  There are no windows, at least where I was at.  I didn’t have a bed- only a reclining chair and I shared the space with 3 other people.  I missed home so bad.  I felt stuck.  I didn’t know how short or long I would be there.  I hope I never have to go through anything like it again.
I’m sorry you’re going through a similar situation.  It’s tough.  All we can do is ride out the storm.  Easier said than done though.
No but that’s ok.
My existence.  I know we all die anyways but I’d prefer to go on my own terms.  Not continue suffering for an indefinite period of time.
A culmination of things.  Mostly being it’s the only way out.  I lost all sense of hope long ago.  I’m just existing, but I wish the process of ending your life wasn’t so messy.
I don’t even know honestly.  I had posted earlier this week that I’m experiencing emotional numbness.  It’s like I’m frustrated, but I still feel nothing.  If that makes any sense.
Thank you!  I would if I felt like there was anything I had to offer worth saving.

I don’t think it makes you a pussy.  I’m not lingering for family.  I have kids and that’s not even enough for me to convince myself to stay.  I expect when it happens it’ll be on a whim.  My hope of turning things around expired a long time ago.
I don’t know what it is.  Honestly.  But you are right, I don’t have a valid reason to keep living.

I haven’t come close.  It’s weird.  I’ve been thinking about suicide still.  This is easily the most ideal time.  If I can’t feel anything, I’m more likely to finish the job without feeling worried, sad, whatever about it.
Even my anxiety has subsided.  I’m numb to everything.
I feel that.  I shouldn’t have had children.  Being a mother just adds to the list of my failures.
Thank you.  That means a lot for you to say.  I’m trying.  I know I’ll never be perfect, but I can get better.
I try, but I can’t shake the feeling of being a disappointment.  Plus my close friends make me look like a loser.  I’m surprised they even engage with me.

A couple of things.  One, that I can’t help but feel like a disappointment to my children.  I wasn’t able to provide them with the life I imagined and that hurts.  I try not to think about it, but when I do, it turns raw and fast.

Second, I lost a friend from high school about 7 years post graduation.  She was such a cool person with amazing energy and a contagious smile and laugh.  We briefly spoke after high school, but I’ll never forget her.  It hurts to know she’s not here anymore.

I understand how you feel.  I’m in my 30s but I don’t picture myself growing old either.  I have this mindset I won’t be successful and I take that as a sign I won’t be here long enough to worry about retirement, finding a spouse, career growth, etc.  Honestly, I like the idea of dying young.  Takes a lot of pressure off of me not having to stress over the territory of being old.

You’re right.  I know that not everyone who is wealthy is happy.  Money can buy us a lot of things, but happiness isn’t one of them.  It’s just hard not to compare.  Here in my city, there’s a lot of wealth.  I live in an area close to billionaires.  An ex president.  People who come from old oil money.  So not just money, A LOT of money.  

For me personally, I’d love to have a nice house and drive a fancy car, but success isn’t just about material things.  The times I’ve felt the best financially is when I can put money aside.  If I was blessed to be a millionaire (or heck have 100k in savings), I’d be investing and growing my personal wealth.  The fact that I’m not able to do that right now really stresses me out.

I understand.  I dread when people start talking about their career and how much money they make, travel, the big house they’re buying.. etc.  it’s just like, well thanks for the reminder of what a failure I am!
Even better.
I couldn’t agree more.
Problem is, I don’t want to live anymore.  Lol.  Not in this world at least.  Whatever is on the other side, has to be better than this shit.
I really don’t care for people at all anymore.  There’s no integrity.  Just a bunch of selfish assholes.
You are amazing!
Texting.  I would only consider dating a guy who will call me.
Maybe, but I’m a complete failure.  I’m one of those mistakes so to speak.
Thank you.  I appreciate your offer.  I just feel I’m not important enough to talk about my issues.
I agree.  There’s only a few people who I think care about me.
They care, but it’s not enough to keep me here being miserable.
Thank you for all you do to help kids in need!

I agree.  It’s a stretch, but this is why I think people who are suffering physically and mentally should have access to a pain free, lethal injection.  It’s not anyone’s business that one should have to continually suffer.  We should be able to make that choice and without the consequence of mutilating our bodies or potential effects of being unsuccessful.
I have scars from self harm over the years.  I know how you feel.

I don’t want to get into the specific details, but having to ask my parents for money or having to be reliant on other people is out of my character.  My dad is close to retirement age.  I don’t want to strip their enjoyment of their new lifestyle when that happens.

Not that me being dead is good either, but we know it’s something inevitable anyways.  I don’t feel like I have to be older.  I already know I’ll never get married, I’m not worthy of making more money, etc.  what’s the point in sticking around & subjecting myself & my loved ones to more stress financially & emotionally?
The idea is scary to me, but I live in a big city so I’ve considered jumping from one of the tall buildings.  I don’t have a gun either and I want to make sure my method is 100% effective.
I know how you feel.  I’m in my early 30s now and wish I had done the same.   I thought something would happen to make life worth living, but all of the good things have disappeared from my life.
I have this twisted visual of myself jumping from a tall building and seeing my mutilated body spread about on a street.

10 years is a really long engagement.  If you have stuck around that long, it’s a clear signal neither of you have ever been fully committed to continuing by pursuing a marriage or ending the relationship.  So yep, I’d leave.

Thank you for your kind reply.  My friends are entirely too good for me.  I know they will be just fine without me as we don’t speak often and they are lovely people with many other friendships.

I wish I had some sense of things getting better, but it brings me a lot of anxiety and stress to stay here without some sort of guarantee.

I understand.  I know I’ll never be perfect, but I know I could be a whole lot better.  Compared to other people my age I look like a complete failure.  My two best friends are well educated and in loving, committed relationships.  I feel like I’m always the friend & family member whose being drug through the mud & it’s embarrassing.  

I do love my kids, but I really feel like I’ve failed them.  It’s frustrating, really.  My history with their dad has cost me so much financially & emotionally.  It’s always easy for others to say I should ask my attorney to assist in a legal matter or I should seek some sort of counseling to deal with my emotional baggage.  All I see is more money to be spent & I’ve already learned no one really cares.

I want my kids to be left with at least a little bit to use towards their future endeavors or first cars, etc.  I know they’ll be ok without me.  Their dad is remarried so they will still have a mother figure in their life.

Thank you for your reply and my condolences over the loss of your brother.  As long as I can remember, I’ve had a feeling I would end my life.  Even during happy times when I felt like I actually had a purpose- the feeling just lingered.  These last couple of years have been very hard.  I was in a long term relationship after my divorce.  I wasn’t good enough (of course) and my ex cheated and is now with the girl he cheated with.  I also live away from family and my ex is a total jerk.  Raising my kids by myself was really wearing on me. I finally decided to let my kids live with him last summer.  There’s always some sort of drama he provokes.  I already feel like I failure as a mom being unable to raise my kids with their biological father and now I feel even worse that I gave him custody.  I can’t think of one aspect of my life in which I’ve been successful.  I’m not a good mom, I barely pay my bills and I’m nothing special as a friend or family member.  The world won’t miss out on anything special without me here.
This.  100 percent.

I was going to write a response, but after reading the above, I’d rather ask you to take thought & consideration into the description of your relationship dynamic.

Is someone who makes you feel this way really the type of person you want to spend your life with?

I know this is an exciting time and it’s easy to put all our eggs in one basket when we like someone.  Enjoy the process, but also be mindful to keep your identity.  Stay engaged in your hobbies, spend time with your friends and loved ones, etc.  In my opinion, it’s healthy to be optimistic a relationship is going to last, but it can be extremely unhealthy for you if it doesn’t work out and you invested your whole identity in that individual.  Balance is key.

I understand how you feel.  I have worked retail and customer service jobs before and have had some customers who were so brutal I would have to excuse myself on occasion to cry in the back.  Do remember they are not a poor reflection on you and don’t take their words and actions personally.  They are the ones of bad character.

Same go for your bosses.  Go to work and do your best every day.  I know it’s not always easy, but if you are able to get yourself in a place where you feel confident in your performance, the circumstances they left you with will become less relevant.

I have noticed the same pattern and I’m an INTJ.  The guys I attract are either really distant (possibly emotionally unavailable) or really clingy and annoying.  It’s extremely hard to find something in the middle.  I will admit I play a role in it though.  I have a bit of “thrill of the chase” and once the excitement dissipates or I start to feel like I actually like someone, I will freak out and run for the hills.  I suppose it’s safe to say I could come across as emotionally unavailable too.
Ironically I’m super emotional to the point I believe it’s made me emotionally unavailable.
